passage: I'm Rekha. For weeks I was sure Mummy and Papa loved my little sister Charu more. They came to her school events, cut her fruit, sat by her bed when she had a cold, and to me they said, "You're big now, you can manage." I began leaving my plate unwashed and answering back, thinking that if I was the trouble one, they might look at me. One evening Papa asked, "Rekha, what is going on?" and I burst out, "You never have time for me." He was quiet, then said Charu needed extra help with reading right now, which did not make me matter less. We planned a Saturday walk just for the two of us.

qa.q: What did Papa and Rekha plan for Saturday?
qa.a: They planned a Saturday walk just for the two of them.

qa.q: Why did Rekha start answering back and leaving plates unwashed?
qa.a: Rekha felt the parents loved Charu more and hoped that being the trouble one would make them notice.

qa.q: What did Rekha do that helped more than acting out?
qa.a: Rekha told Papa honestly, "You never have time for me," which led to a regular walk for the two of them.

qa.q: How might Papa see the difference between Rekha's and Charu's needs?
qa.a: Papa sees that Charu needs extra help with reading right now, which does not mean Rekha is loved less.

grounding: A child feels a sibling is favoured, acts out, then tells the father and gets one-to-one time.

passage:
"Mummy, you never come to my football matches anymore."
"Jasleen, you know Kiran's arm is in a cast. He needs help with everything."
"But it's always Kiran. You sit with him, you cut his food, you help with his homework."
"Because he can't do those things right now."
"I know. But I feel like you love him more."
Mummy put down the spoon. "Oh, Jasleen. I don't. His needs are different right now. Not bigger than you."
"Can we have time, just us? Even a bit?"
"Saturday morning. Just us. I'll come to your match."
Jasleen hugged her. "Okay."

qa.q: Why does Kiran need so much help right now?
qa.a: His arm is in a cast.

qa.q: What was Jasleen feeling about Mummy's attention to Kiran?
qa.a: She felt left out and jealous, as if Mummy loved Kiran more.

qa.q: What did Jasleen do that was wise?
qa.a: She told Mummy honestly how she felt and asked for one-to-one time, rather than acting up.

qa.q: How might Mummy feel when Jasleen says she feels less loved?
qa.a: Mummy seems surprised and sad, quickly reassuring her that Kiran's needs are just different right now.

grounding: A girl feels her parents love her brother more because he gets more attention; she says what she feels and asks for one-to-one time.

passage:
I'm Ira. The year my brother Sachin had his Class 10 boards, the whole house revolved around him. Quiet in the evenings. His favourite food every night. Papa sitting up with him until late.
Nobody asked about my science fair model. I felt invisible, and once I even broke a glass on purpose, just so someone would look at me.
Then one night I sat next to Papa. "It feels like you love Sachin more."
Papa put his arm around me. "He needs more help right now because of his exams. It's not more love."
"Can we do something together? Just us?"
We started walking to the market together every Sunday.

qa.q: Why did Ira break a glass on purpose?
qa.a: Ira felt invisible and jealous, wanting someone in the family to notice.

qa.q: What did Ira do that helped more than breaking things?
qa.a: Ira told Papa honestly how it felt and asked for time together, which led to Sunday walks.

qa.q: How might Papa see the extra attention Sachin gets?
qa.a: Papa sees it as meeting Sachin's needs during exams, not as loving him more.

grounding: A child feels the parents love the brother more because he gets more attention during exams; instead of acting up, Ira says so and asks for one-to-one time.
